neighbours.label: biblical or gospel narrative text (parables, Jesus' sayings, scripture style)
fire: And Jesus said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel.
The disciples asked him, Master, who sinned, this man or his parents?
Then the Pharisees went out and plotted how they might trap him in his words.
He told them a parable: a sower went out to sow his seed in the field.
Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth, said the Lord.
Mary stood weeping outside the tomb, and the angels asked why she wept.
The prodigal son came to himself and said, I will arise and go to my father.
Jesus answered the lawyer, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
quiet: And the coach told the players to go out and win the match for the town.
The students asked the professor whether the exam would cover chapter nine.
Then the senators went out and planned how they might delay the vote.
He told them a story about a farmer who planted corn in the spring.
Happy are the patient, for they will find a parking spot, said the driver.
Mary stood waiting outside the office, and the clerk asked why she came.
The young man came home and said, I will look for a job with my father.
The judge answered the lawyer that the hearing would resume on Monday.

notes: Card: weak pole (max 5.7), mixed tokens; top examples are scripture: 'say long prayers' (Mark 12), 'responding to a lawyer' (Matthew 22), 'Woman, why are you crying?' (John 20), 'enough money to pay him' (Luke 7). Near misses are secular narratives with similar words.
